findings.evidence: The observation states "There is diffuse bilateral patchy opacification, which is more prominent in the lower lung zones. This pattern of opacification is not typical for lobar consolidation." While not typical lobar consolidation, the presence of diffuse bilateral patchy opacification suggests that stating "No lobar consolidation" is misleading as it implies a clear lung, which is not the case. The observation also mentions "bilateral pleural effusions," which can obscure or mimic consolidation.

The observation explicitly states "There is also evidence of bilateral pleural effusions, more pronounced on the right." The candidate report states "No appreciable pleural effusion or pneumothorax," which contradicts the observation regarding pleural effusion.

verdict.limitations: The semi-upright position and single lateral view may limit the full assessment of lung volumes, extent of atelectasis, and subtle parenchymal changes. The diffuse nature of opacities makes it difficult to definitively exclude small areas of consolidation. The images are semi-upright and may not fully demonstrate the extent of pleural effusions or subtle consolidations.
